newsitem.title: GERMANY: Nervy German shares pressured by Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Nervy German shares pressured by Wall Street.

text.p: German shares pared back some of their sharp losses by the close of late trade on Friday but concerns about further global stock market weakness kept prices under pressure and kep attention fixed on Wall Street.
The IBIS DAX index ended the post-bourse trading session down 31.17 points at 2,815.77, some 16 points above the mid-day DAX bourse session close at 2,799.71, a drop of 1.7 percent.
The DAX's slide followed Thursday's 100-point tumble on the Dow Jones index -- the biggest since July -- which triggered memories of last Friday's markets rout.
"We had Wall Street, we had this technical problem and it's Friday the 13th as well," said a Dusseldorf dealer.
"We all got a wee bit nervous. People aren't sure if we are going into a weak phase for stocks or not," he added.
A rocky start on Wall Street Friday added to the confusion as the Dow Jones index first dipped, then turned higher.

The German futures market was an early cause for concern as the December DAX futures contract tumbled below the crucial 2,800-point level. Futures were down 54 points at 2,796 at the mid-day floor close, but climbed higher to end the afternoon session down 30.5 at 2,819.5.
"Fundamentally, there is no real justification for the German market to be under this kind of pressure," another dealer said. "But we just can't get away from Wall Street."
There was minimal focus on corporate news.

Among the few blue chip stock to buck the downward trend was carmaker Volkswagen, which was upgraded to "outperform" from "neutral" by Lehman Brothers despite the damaging publicity it is facing over criminal charges against its former management board member, Jose Ignacio Lopez de Arriortua.
Volkswagen ended the bourse session up 3.75 marks at 603.75 and rose to 606.90 marks in electronic dealings. The biggest decliners were chemical stocks, which had been pushed up in recent days.
Early dealings were further marred by technical problems at the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, which blocked dealings for over an hour in the pre-bourse session and damaged market sentiment.
A central computer failure meant stock trading was impossible from 0815 GMT through to 1025 GMT.
